description: checkout-service v2.4.1 leaks Redis connections, as in S1. 150 s later order-service v1.8.1 starts serving with a cache that misses two lookups in five, each miss slower than checkout's attempt timeout. Rolling checkout back ends the leak, but checkout keeps failing on order-service, so recovery is not reached and Sentinel investigates again.

cause.description: Deployment of order-service v1.8.1, whose cache misses outlast checkout's attempt timeout: the cause that remains once the checkout-service v2.4.1 leak is rolled back.

confounders.description: checkout-service v2.4.1, a real cause that the first cycle rolls back; it no longer serves when the follow-up cycle begins.

expectedObservations.description: checkout-service's own Redis connections climb after v2.4.1 serves.
Checkout SLO burn rate crosses the detection threshold.
order-service p95 latency passes checkout's attempt timeout once v1.8.1 serves.

discriminatingSignals.description: Redis connections held by checkout-service itself grow after v2.4.1 serves: the first cause.
order-service p95 latency stays low until v1.8.1 serves, so the first cycle's window holds no second cause.
Checkout gives up on order-service once v1.8.1 serves.

noise.notes: Request pacing, query latency and order-service's cache misses use seeded jitter. The first cycle's approval decides when the first recovery window opens. The baseline expectation follows the scenario's own steps; in the follow-up cycle the latest deployment can be Sentinel's own rollback of checkout-service, which the baseline would undo, redeploying the leak.

leading.cause: order-service v1.8.1 slowed order-service past checkout's attempt timeout

rejected.cause: checkout-service v2.4.1, already rolled back, still causes the symptoms
the rollback to checkout-service v2.4.0 caused the symptoms

recovery.restoredBy: rollback checkout-service to v2.4.0, then order-service to v1.7.0

criteria.description: order-service p95 latency back under checkout's attempt timeout.
